key_insight: Bubble nucleation can be a collective, scale-separated process: nearby sites stabilize each other through hydrodynamic shielding, while larger-spacing interactions control vapor removal and departure.
engineering_relevance: Designing cavity pairs with tuned spacing can make boiling surfaces more reliable and higher-performing by controlling site activation stability and bubble removal regime independently.
method: Built boiling surfaces with cavity pairs.
Varied intra-pair spacing at boundary-layer scale and inter-pair spacing at departure-diameter scale.
Separated near-wall nucleation effects from collective vapor-removal dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reduced nucleation variability and sustained activity for closely spaced sites, plus distinct excessive, promotive, and isolated departure regimes as spacing changes.
watch_item: The multiscale design appears geometry- and regime-dependent, so transfer to other fluids, heat fluxes, or surface materials may require re-tuning.
paper_title: Collective Bubble Nucleation: Scale-Separated Hydrodynamic Control of Site Stability and Vapor Removal
